extracted.intended_audience: research community (authors, reviewers, editors) and journal stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for implementing and operating transparent peer review across journals, including publishing reviewer reports, optional signing, and experimenting with peer review models to increase transparency, diversity and reviewer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of reviewer reports for all peer reviewed content
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC will implement the publication of reviewer reports for all peer reviewed content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transition is being implemented across BMC Series titles in stages (complete by Q4 2020). Publishing reviewer reports is presented as a core policy change to increase transparency of the review process and show readers the process behind editorial decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional signing of reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing of reviewer reports will be optional — reviewers may choose to remain anonymous or to sign their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers who wish to continue to sign their reports are welcome to, and their names will remain linked to their contributions. Making signing optional aims to remove a barrier to participation and to allow reviewers to choose anonymity if they prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show editorial decision-making process to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use transparent peer review workflows to show readers the process behind editorial decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making the editorial process visible is framed as increasing accountability and helping readers understand how decisions were reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase accountability through transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency of reviewer reports increases accountability in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing reports is argued to increase accountability of editors and reviewers and to provide an improved service for authors by making the review history visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of editors and peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent peer review helps recognise the work of editors and peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewers sign reports, their contributions are publicly associated and recognised. Even anonymous published reports can increase recognition of the review process itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote diversity in the reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy aims to promote diversity within the reviewer pool as part of implementing transparent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By removing the mandate to sign reports and offering choices, BMC expects to broaden engagement from potential reviewers across different backgrounds and career stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase reviewer uptake by allowing anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing the requirement for reviewers to sign reports is expected to increase reviewer uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog cites evidence and feedback suggesting mandatory signing can be an impediment, especially for potential reviewers who might otherwise decline to participate. Allowing anonymity should help secure reviewer panels more efficiently for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support early career researchers' participation and candour
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing anonymous peer reviews and not mandating signing will better support early career researchers to engage in peer review and be candid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence suggests early career researchers feel reluctant to participate or to be as candid if names will be publicly shared. Allowing anonymity aims to increase their participation and the candour of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve review quality and confidence in the process
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent peer review is expected to lead to an improvement in review quality and increase overall confidence that the peer review process is working effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing review reports provides visibility that can improve quality and trust in peer review; this is an asserted benefit of the policy change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentation with varied peer review models
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue experimenting with different peer review models (open peer review, double-blind, results-free peer review, portable peer review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC describes a history of experimenting with multiple models since 1999 and positions continued experimentation as part of aligning transparency with author/reviewer needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide tailored services to support community needs and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Align transparency goals with providing tailored services that support reviewer and author needs, development, and engagement with journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The move towards transparent peer review is presented alongside a commitment to provide better tailored services to support the research community’s needs and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community consultation and feedback-guided implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement changes in consultation with the research community and be guided by community feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog emphasizes continuing consultation as changes are rolled out, acknowledging disciplinary differences and seeking community support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged rollout acknowledging disciplinary variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Roll out transparent peer review across journals in stages, recognizing that adoption may take time across different disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC will move journals across in stages (complete by Q4 2020) and notes that changes may take time to be fully supported across different disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher responsibility to support the global scholarly community
rubrics_metrics.description: As a global publisher, BMC has responsibility to support the scholarly community in promoting transparency while creating constructive environments for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a policy principle motivating the change: balance transparency with support for reviewers so they feel valued and able to provide honest constructive feedback.
